commands.cmd:
python3 -c 'import re; from pathlib import Path; s=Path("skills/agent-bus/SKILL.md").read_text(); d=Path("docs/vps-agent-bus.md").read_text();
for t in ["agent_bus_health","agent_bus_start_job","agent_bus_get_job","agent_bus_wait_job"]:
    assert t in s and t in d, t
assert s.startswith("---\nname: agent-bus\ndescription: ")
for name,txt in (("skill",s),("doc",d)):
    plain=txt.replace("**","").lower(); assert "hermes-mcp-bridge.mjs" in plain, name; assert "uninstall" in plain, name; assert "handoff_to_hermes" in txt, name; assert "draft pr" in plain, name; assert re.search(r"do not (rebuild|recreate|reinstall)", plain), name
assert "Never in a goal, PR, receipt, commit, or chat" in s
assert "not part of the tool result" in d
assert "/v1/jobs" in d
assert not re.search(r"(?i)(api[_-]?key|BUS_TOKEN\s*=|Bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9])", s+d)
print("ok")'

claims.claim: The ownership manifest still validates after the change: 7 bots, 90 rules, no duplicate patterns.

G-1 passes for bot-00-programming-lead on every path this branch touches. The two new paths resolve to bot-00 through the existing docs/vps-agent-bus.md and skills/agent-bus/** rules, so no rule dangles and no path is unowned.
G-3 reports no secret in the three changed non-receipt files. No bus token, wss credential, or API key was written.

Both files name the four live agent_bus_* tools, keep the skill frontmatter shape the pack uses, record that stdio user-hermes stays uninstalled and hermes-mcp-bridge.mjs is not rebuilt, state the GitHub draft PR as the durable output, and contain no credential literal.
ownership.yaml is unchanged from origin/main — the manifest already matched both new paths, so nothing needed editing there.

The diff against origin/main on the complete branch is four paths — skills/agent-bus/SKILL.md, docs/vps-agent-bus.md, docs/intake-e2e-runbook.md, and this receipt — all owned by bot-00. The earlier wording named only the first three because the evidence command had been run before the receipt was committed.
G-2 fails closed on this receipt while approved_by is empty. That empty field is intentional — LEAD does not self-approve. It is not a completed approval and not a passing gate.

G-1 no longer passes for bot-00-programming-lead across everything this branch changes: skills/README.md is bot-06-quality-security's and was added on operator instruction. The round-1 content fixes themselves are unaffected -- the jobId-before-waiting rule, the idempotency_key qualification and the timeout_sec/poll_sec alignment are all still asserted by the content check, and the four originally-owned paths still pass G-1 on their own.
G-1 still passes for bot-00-programming-lead on the complete four-path branch after the round-1 fixes. No path moved outside bot-00 ownership.
No secret was introduced by the Greptile round. G-3 passes on the complete four-path branch.

The extended content assertions pass: the jobId-before-waiting rule is present in both files, neither presents idempotency_key as retry protection, and agent_bus_wait_job now uses the live descriptor's timeout_sec and poll_sec names instead of the looser 'timeout default 180s' phrasing.

The runbook no longer contradicts itself about these two paths. Greptile cited line 146; four further places said the same thing (the BUS_TOKEN paragraph, both ownership-table rows, and the unverified list) and all five are corrected, so no surviving line tells an operator the skill is absent.

G-1 FAILS for bot-00-programming-lead on this branch because skills/README.md is owned by bot-06-quality-security. The operator instructed LEAD to add the agent-bus index row anyway after being told twice that it is a cross-seat edit. This is a deliberate, recorded ownership violation, not an accident and not a gate that was worked around: the gate was run, it failed, and the failure is reported here. QUALITY owns the decision to accept it, waive it, or split the row into its own bot-06 PR.
The violation is confined to that one path. G-1 passes for bot-00-programming-lead on the other four files this branch changes, so nothing else crossed a seat boundary.
skills/README.md resolves to bot-06-quality-security, which is the seat that could have made this edit without a G-1 failure. The manifest was not modified to make the path LEAD-owned.
G-3 reports no secret across all five changed files, including skills/README.md.

reproducibility_check.method: Every string in commands[].cmd was extracted from this receipt and re-executed with bash -c from the repo root, comparing each actual exit code against the recorded one.
reproducibility_check.result: All 15 commands re-execute with their recorded exit codes, including four intentional non-zero entries (index 6, G-2 failing closed while approved_by is empty; index 7 and index 11, G-1 failing FOREIGN on skills/README.md; index 10, the grep finding no match, which is the wanted result).
reproducibility_check.not_recorded_as_a_command: This sweep is deliberately not itself an entry in commands[]: a command that re-executes every command in the receipt would include itself and recurse without terminating.
reproducibility_check.prompted_by: Greptile round 2 P1, comment 4137232677 — commands[9] had held a prose paraphrase in angle brackets with a recorded exit_code of 0, which a reviewer could not reproduce and which G-2 would have accepted on the recorded exit code alone.
reproducibility_check.drift_caught: Re-running the sweep after the skills/README.md edit caught commands[7] recording exit 0 while actually exiting 1. Two causes compounded: the branch gained a path bot-00 does not own, and the command interpolated a floating origin/main that had advanced to 0a35be6. Both are fixed in that entry rather than left as a green record of a red gate.
